summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with acute-on-chronic epigastric pain and nausea, shortly after a prior discharge from bariatric surgery. Labs and imaging were unremarkable, with no evidence of obstruction or infection. She was managed medically with NPO status, IV fluids, IV pantoprazole, and pain control. Tube feeds were continued, and she gradually advanced to clear and full liquids without emesis. New medications—erythromycin and rifaximin—were added to address possible bacterial overgrowth and dysmotility, and ranitidine was initiated for reflux. The patient’s pain stabilized, and she was discharged home with a plan to continue tube feeds, oral medications, and close follow-up with bariatric surgery to review H. pylori results and adjust treatment as needed.
